Take this free CAT Logarithms online test — 10 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring and a worked explanation for every answer. The Logarithms chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Logarithms tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Logarithms

The laws of logarithms, change of base, number of digits and log-based equations.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • logₐ(mn) = logₐm + logₐn; logₐ(mᵏ) = k·logₐm.
  • Change of base: logₐm = log m / log a.
  • a^(logₐm) = m; logₐa = 1, logₐ1 = 0.
  • Digits in N = ⌊log₁₀N⌋ + 1.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Writing log(m+n) as logm + logn (only products split).
  • Ignoring the domain (arguments > 0, base > 0 and ≠ 1).
  • Base-change errors.

questions.q: How many values of x satisfy log₄(x) = logˣ(4)?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Let log₄(x) = t. Then logˣ(4) = 1/t (reciprocal identity).
Step 2: t = 1/t ⇒ t² = 1 ⇒ t = 1 or t = −1.
Step 3: t=1: x = 4¹ = 4; t=−1: x = 4^(−1) = 1/4. Two valid solutions.
Answer: 2

faq.q: Does log(a+b) equal log a + log b?
faq.a: No. Only products split: log(ab) = log a + log b. Sums do not simplify.

faq.q: How to count digits of a big power?
faq.a: Digits = ⌊log₁₀N⌋ + 1; take log₁₀, use log₁₀2 ≈ 0.301 and log₁₀3 ≈ 0.477.
